root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: von Hennig Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Bc4

overview: After 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 White plays 4.Bc4 instead of recapturing on e4. The idea is to meet 4...Nf6 with attacks on f7 and quick development for the pawn. Black can usually play ...Nf6 or ...e6 and keep the extra pawn, so the line is rare and unsound-looking.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Bc4, Nge2 or Nf3, aiming at f7
Use the lead in development to attack before Black consolidates
Recover the e4 pawn when it is safe

black_ideas.idea: Trade pieces and convert the extra pawn

typical_structures.structure: Caro-Kann with Black a pawn up and White ahead in development; open centre

character.notes: White is a pawn down and plays for traps on f7.

gambit.notes: The e4 pawn stays with Black unless White recovers it by force.

structure.notes: Semi-open Caro-Kann structure with the d-pawns exchanged.

level.notes: Gambit not a good first repertoire choice.

character.reason: White gambits a pawn for fast development and attacking chances.

gambit.reason: Black can keep the pawn after 4.Bc4.

soundness.reason: Black has simple ways to hold the pawn.

structure.reason: Caro-Kann structure with the d-file half open.

level.reason: Dubious so never Beginner; little to memorise.

plans.reason: White plays for development and pressure on f7.
